stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: Process the IDs in original order. For each digit position, group earlier IDs by all other digits. A transition can change only that digit, and the best previous score plus absolute digit difference equals the maximum of stored(score+digit)-current and stored(score-digit)+current. Compute all transitions for the current ID before updating any group, preserving chronological order. Retain fixed-width digit strings, duplicates and leading zeros; the initial remembered ID contributes score0.
stdio_review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.
stdio_review.reviewer: current Codex assistant, candidate author and explicit source/algorithm reviewer

stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: Covering all attractions by vertex-disjoint directed cycles is equivalent to assigning each vertex exactly one outgoing and one incoming edge. Excluding self-assignments enforces cycle length at least2. Solve this minimum-cost perfect bipartite matching using Hungarian augmentations, and report N when no finite augmenting assignment exists. Directed edge costs remain asymmetric and duplicate roads retain their least cost; multiple input graphs are parsed through their0 terminators.
